evidence.note: Title claims a time reduction: returns take three days instead of eleven.
Diagram is a plain Return request -> Warehouse -> Refund flow with no durations or before/after comparison, so it does not show the three-vs-eleven point.
A numbered three-step text list on the left repeats the diagram's stages in prose.
A column of three quote tiles (Customer, Warehouse lead, Finance) sits to the right, adding a third parallel element.
Caption 'Median days, January to March, all regions' labels data that no visible chart shows.
At the smaller viewport the title, step list, diagram, quote column and caption are all crammed side by side across the width.

rationale: The title's message (three days instead of eleven) is not carried by the visual, which shows only a process flow, so title and visual do not point the same way. The slide stacks a title, numbered step list, diagram, quote-tile column and an orphaned data caption, matching the fail anchor's crowded layout. A viewer would need to read everything to reconcile the elements rather than grasp one point at a glance.
